\subsection{What the Memory State Carries}
\label{sec:exp_memory}

\textbf{Question.} Two follow-ups to RQ1: how many past readings the state needs, and whether the gain from memory is inter-turn dynamics or a fixed offset per prompt item.
\textbf{Setup.} Tasks, baselines and the skill score follow \S\ref{sec:exp_setup}; both experiments vary one thing in the KOMPAS (linear) row of Table~\ref{tab:prediction}.
Table~\ref{tab:prediction} fits each row on every transition its state can be formed from, so a one-reading state trains on earlier turns than a four-reading state.  % paper_side_experiments_results.md section 1.2, default caliber
Both experiments here fit every depth on the same set of transitions, which separates the depth of the state from the size of its training set.  % matched caliber; figs/_fig_report.json
Under that matched window the memory gain on sentence length shrinks from +0.603 in Table~\ref{tab:prediction} to +0.109, so the two calibers answer different questions.  % n_main_013 (default) vs n_abl_127 (matched)

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figs/fig_memory_depth.pdf}
\caption{Memory depth under a matched training window. (a) Paired $\mathrm{Skill}_H$ gain of a state holding $d$ past readings over a state holding one, on the four tasks whose design allows a sweep. (b) The same gain for one extra reading on the three tasks whose design allows two depths. Filled markers: the 95\% paired bootstrap interval excludes zero.}
\label{fig:memory_depth}
\end{figure}

\textbf{Findings, depth.} On three of the four sweepable tasks the second reading buys the whole gain: +0.112 on sentence length, +0.228 on items (s2), +0.127 on items (s1).  % c10; n_abl_124 n_abl_184 n_abl_157
The third and fourth readings add no more than 0.010 on those three tasks.  % n_abl_126 n_abl_128 n_abl_186 n_abl_188 n_abl_159 n_abl_161
The items (s1) interval contains zero at every depth.  % n_abl_157 n_abl_158 n_abl_160
Constraint is the exception: each added turn keeps paying, +0.149, +0.054 and +0.027 for the second, third and fourth, each with an interval excluding zero.  % n_abl_235 n_abl_237 n_abl_239
Of the three two-depth tasks, sentiment gains +0.155 from one extra reading, while defense and CEFR do not separate from zero.  % n_abl_151 (caveated: two cells) n_abl_245 n_abl_262
The driver is that a level and a trend take two readings to express, and the attribute tasks carry little structure beyond that pair.  % m1
No mechanism is established for why constraint keeps gaining, and none is proposed here.  % c10 notes

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figs/fig_item_effect.pdf}
\caption{What the memory gain decomposes into. For each task of Table~\ref{tab:prediction}, three paired $\mathrm{Skill}_H$ differences under the matched window: the memory gain of KOMPAS (linear) over Last-turn; the part recovered by adding a per-item intercept to Last-turn; and the remainder of KOMPAS (linear) over Last-turn with that intercept. Intercepts are estimated on turns outside the scored window. Filled markers: the 95\% interval excludes zero.}
\label{fig:item_effect}
\end{figure}

\textbf{Findings, item intercept.} A per-item intercept added to the one-reading state recovers most of the memory gain: 81\% on constraint and 67\% on items (s2).  % c11; n_mech_061/n_mech_060=0.807, n_mech_058/n_mech_057=0.673
What remains after the intercept is +0.045 on constraint and +0.075 on items (s2), both with intervals excluding zero.  % n_mech_059 n_mech_056
On the other five tasks the remainder does not separate from zero, and on sentiment and items (s1) the intercept accounts for the whole gain.  % n_mech_050 n_mech_053 n_mech_047 n_mech_068 n_mech_062; n_mech_052 vs n_mech_051, n_mech_055 vs n_mech_054
The driver is that each prompt item holds its own level across turns, and several past readings estimate that level where one reading cannot.  % m6
Inter-turn dynamics beyond that level is measured on two tasks, and it is the smaller of the two parts on both.  % c11 notes

Together, \uline{one extra reading carries most of what memory buys, and most of that is a per-item level rather than inter-turn dynamics. A remainder attributable to dynamics is measured on two of seven tasks.}
